proof:
# Tilted-volume boundary concentration with uniformly interior contact sources

This is an actual changing-body counterexample to automatic uniform integrability of the inverse parameter. It has positive affine log-normalized parameters, exact one-source volume contact certificates, uniformly interior source marks, uniformly bounded parameter maxima and source values bounded away from zero. Nevertheless a nonzero tilted-volume atom develops at a boundary point where the limiting parameter vanishes.

The original-volume rows remain exactly uniform and converge without an atom. The selected sources are **not** deepest points. No physical separator or joint body minimum is claimed. Thus this does not refute a possible additional conclusion using actual deepestness or physical criticality.

## 1. Actual bodies, parameters, and exact integrals

Let d=2, n=0, and let m>=8 be an integer. Define

    a=1/m, eta=2^(−m), b=a−eta, U=1−b,
    K_m={(x,y):x>=0, y>=0, a<=x+y<=1},
    V_m=|K_m|=(1−a^2)/2,
    ell_m(x,y)=x+y−b.

These are positive convex bodies converging in Hausdorff distance to the standard triangle K={x,y>=0,x+y<=1}. The affine parameter ell_m has minimum eta>0 and maximum U<1. Put

    c_m=exp[−V_m^(−1) integral_(K_m) log ell_m],
    L_m=c_m ell_m.

Thus V_m^(−1) integral log L_m=0 exactly. In the coordinates x=t s, y=t(1−s), 0<=s<=1, the area element is t dt ds. Consequently

    Z_m:=integral_(K_m) ell_m^(−1)
       =1−a+b log(U/eta),                              (1)
    I_m:=integral_a^1 t^2/(t−b) dt
       =V_m+b(1−a)+b^2 log(U/eta).                    (2)

In particular

    I_m−b Z_m=V_m.                                    (3)

For the normalization integral, an exact primitive after the substitution s=t−b is

    G_b(s)=s^2 log s/2−s^2/4+b(s log s−s),
    integral_(K_m) log ell_m=G_b(U)−G_b(eta).           (4)

As m tends to infinity, a,b,eta tend to zero, b m tends to one, and U tends to one. Equations (1)–(4) give

    Z_m ->1+log 2,  I_m ->1/2,  V_m ->1/2,
    c_m ->exp(1/2).                                   (5)

For (4), the lower-end terms tend to zero: eta^2|log eta| tends to zero and b eta|log eta| tends to zero. The upper-end expression tends to −1/4. No limit of unbounded integrands is presumed without these exact evaluations.

## 2. Exact one-source contact certificate

Define the probability law and its actual mean by

    d rho_m=dm/[Z_m ell_m],
    Y_m=(I_m/(2Z_m), I_m/(2Z_m)).                      (6)

Let L_i,m=L_m(Y_m). Equation (3) gives

    L_i,m=c_m V_m/Z_m,
    E_(rho_m) w=Y_m,  E_(rho_m) L_m=L_i,m,
    rho_m/L_i,m=dm/(V_m L_m).                         (7)

Thus sigma=1 supplies the exact tilted-volume contact row, with an affine touching plane equal to L_m everywhere. Its original-volume version is

    d bar rho_m=(L_m/L_i,m)d rho_m=dm/V_m.             (8)

This is also a genuine fixed-mark global parameter certificate. If a positive concave U is log-normalized on K_m, concavity at the mean Y_m and Jensen for log give

    integral_(bar rho_m) log(U/L_m)
      <=log[integral_(rho_m) U/L_i,m]
      <=log[U(Y_m)/L_i,m].                            (9)

The first step uses bar rho_m=(L_m/L_i,m)rho_m and the convex-perspective form of Jensen, equivalently Jensen under bar rho_m followed by integral_(bar rho_m)(U/L_m)=integral_(rho_m)U/L_i,m. The left side is zero. Hence U(Y_m)>=L_i,m. Equality forces U/L_m constant almost everywhere and normalization makes that constant one. This asserts optimality for the prescribed mark only; it does not make that mark deepest for the buffered or ordinary body problem.

## 3. Uniform bounds, including an actual source ball

For m>=8, eta<a and 0<b<a<=1/8. Since U<1,

    7/8<=1−a<=Z_m<1−a+b m<2.

Here log(U/eta)<m log 2<m. Likewise

    63/128<=V_m<=I_m<1/2+2a<=3/4.

It follows that each coordinate of Y_m lies between 63/512 and 3/7. The lower diagonal slack is

    (Y_m)_1+(Y_m)_2−a >=31/256,

and the upper diagonal slack is at least 1/7. After dividing these slacks by sqrt(2), and also considering the two coordinate facets, one obtains the explicit uniform inclusion

    B(Y_m,1/32) subset K_m.                           (10)

Because ell_m<1, c_m>=1. The logarithmic concave-maximum inequality in dimension two gives log max L_m<=H_2=3/2. Therefore

    max_(K_m)L_m<=exp(3/2),
    L_i,m=c_m V_m/Z_m>=63/256,
    integral_(K_m) dm/(V_m L_m)<=256/63.              (11)

The last bound follows from Z_m/(V_m c_m). In particular neither lack of a source inball nor unbounded total tilted mass explains the concentration below. The parameters are single affine planes, and their coefficients converge; this is not a proliferation of parameter facets.

## 4. Exact weak limit and failure of uniform integrability

For any continuous test function phi on a fixed compact neighborhood of K,

    integral_(K_m) phi/ell_m
      =integral_a^1 integral_0^1 phi(ts,t(1−s)) ds dt
       +b integral_a^1 integral_0^1
            phi(ts,t(1−s))/(t−b) ds dt.               (12)

The first term tends to integral_K phi/(x+y) dm. Its total mass is one. The second term has total mass b log(U/eta), tending to log 2. For any fixed delta>0 its part at t>=delta has mass bounded by

    b log[(1−b)/(delta−b)] ->0.

Uniform continuity of phi then identifies its entire weak limit as (log 2)phi(0). Thus, as finite measures on a common ambient compact set,

    dm_(K_m)/ell_m
       converges weakly to dm_K/(x+y)+(log 2)delta_(0,0). (13)

Consequently

    rho_m -> [dm_K/(x+y)+(log 2)delta_(0,0)]/(1+log 2),
    dm_(K_m)/(V_m L_m)
       ->2 exp(−1/2)[dm_K/(x+y)+(log 2)delta_(0,0)].    (14)

But L_m converges uniformly, as an affine function on a common bounded set, to

    L_infinity=exp(1/2)(x+y).

The naive density dm_K/(|K| L_infinity) is only the absolutely continuous part of the second measure in (14). It misses a positive atom of mass 2 exp(−1/2)log 2. This proves failure of uniform integrability even under all the bounds in (10)–(11).

By contrast (8) converges to dm_K/|K|. Multiplying the tilted rows by L_m/L_i,m removes the boundary defect, since its limiting support lies where L_infinity=0. The limiting tilted mean remains

    Y_infinity=(1/[4(1+log 2)],1/[4(1+log 2)]),         (15)

whereas the original-volume mean tends to (1/3,1/3). Deleting the atom and renormalizing the remaining tilted law would instead give mean (1/4,1/4), so even the tilted barycenter cannot be recovered that way.

## 5. Precise obstruction and deepestness limitation

The example disproves the inference

    bounded L_max + positive source values + uniform source cores
    + exact volume contact rows + bounded inverse mass
    => uniform integrability of dm/L.

It does not disprove a statement adding actual deepestness or the full SAME physical separator. Indeed the limiting source in (15) is far from deepest in the triangle. The halfspace x+y<=2(Y_infinity)_1 contains it and captures the normalized mass

    1/[4(1+log 2)^2] <1/4<4/9,

while the triangle centroid has ordinary depth 4/9. Hausdorff continuity preserves this strict source-depth gap for all sufficiently large m. Thus the prescribed contact certificate cannot be substituted for an actual deepest-source certificate.

Nor does (13) contradict the scaled surface-log vanishing theorem. Here the unscaled inverse gradient remains bounded: integral |grad log L_m|=sqrt(2) Z_m. A vanishing force multiplier can still make its volume and surface logarithmic contributions vanish, while the unscaled inverse-density measures retain the atom.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_truncated_triangle_tilted_atom_slab_recovery.py` checks the exact primitives, contact normalization identity, rational geometry bounds, and the finite parameter inequalities. The weak convergence and missing-atom conclusions are proved analytically in Section 4, not inferred from samples.
